issues.note: Six protocol revisions are pinned: the SDK's five negotiable legacy revisions (2024-10-07, 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25) reached via the initialize handshake, and 2026-07-28 reached via server/discover plus the per-request _meta envelope. tests/protocol/conformanceMatrix.ts declares one explicit cell per revision x behavior; tests/protocol/conformance.test.ts drives the real createMcpHandler once per pinned cell across ten behaviors (revision negotiation, capability negotiation, undeclared capabilities staying unserved, tool surface, tool schemas, error vocabulary, era-specific result fields, cancellation, JSON-RPC batching, Streamable HTTP transport) = 60 conformant cells. Not-pinned is a third state, never collapsed into either result: resolveCell reaches 'conformant' only from a pinned declaration whose fixture ran AND passed, a pinned cell with no executing fixture resolves to 'unproven' and fails the gate, and MCP Tasks / MCP Apps are declared not_pinned with reasons rather than omitted. scripts/conformance-matrix.ts is the gate — it binds vitest results back to cells via the [conformance <revision> <behavior>] token and fails on an unproven cell, a failing cell, an orphan fixture, a failed check bound to no cell (how revision drift surfaces), or a stale docs/PROTOCOL_CONFORMANCE.md. All four failure modes were exercised live before landing. CI runs the gate as a named step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The published matrix names revisions and behaviors and quotes no coverage percentage, and keeps supported / merged / conformance-proven apart.

issues.note: src/lib/runnerEligibility.ts judges seven capability dimensions (runtime location, credential custody, network exposure, lifecycle control, cancellation, audit trail, approval enforcement) against a declared posture, as a strict attended < unattended < public ratchet. Absent evidence and negative evidence never share a code path: no record scores unproven -> needs_evidence, a negative record scores refuted -> ineligible. An attestation without a source counts in neither direction; a malformed record is absence, never a refusal. Fails closed — no/empty/malformed profile returns needs_evidence, and no input yields eligible without a positive sourced record for every required dimension. Reachability is recorded but is deliberately not an input to the decision. export_build_brief takes runner_posture (default 'public'), runner_reachable, and runner_capability_profile, and exports the decision plus per-dimension evidence as the runner_eligibility field and in §9 for runner-hostable targets only. Presence/absence fixture pairs cover every required dimension at every posture. Compact-response size ceiling raised 90 KB -> 96 KB deliberately: the canonical compact response was already at 98.3% of the old budget, so the evidence could not fit under it.

issues.note: Found by LAB's promotion-queue session (/promote, orchestratelab PR #58) by doing it and reverting: promoting a playbook past its still-candidate golden-path route made loadRegistry({ includeBeta: true }) throw 'Unknown route id' for EVERY caller (not just the one playbook), and validate_playbook_candidate read playbooks only — nothing in the MCP could certify a route at all. Fixed both halves, the atomic-pair option (not 'route inherits playbook certification'), since it is the one that keeps loadRegistry structurally unbreakable by a half-promotion. (1) src/registry/registryValidation.ts + registryAssembly.ts: validateCrossReferences resolves golden_path_route_id against the full unfiltered route set first; a route that exists but is invisible only at the current status filter is now a severity:'warning' entry that never fails a strict load (a genuinely unknown route id is still a hard error). (2) A new CI/lint gate, lintPlaybookRouteStatusOrder in registryLint.ts, makes the drift impossible to land in the first place. It deliberately does NOT use a raw status-rank comparison: src/registry/lifecycleStatus.ts's routeLagsBehindPlaybook models the real constraint that beta/candidate are gated behind two INDEPENDENT loadRegistry flags (includeBeta, includeCandidates) while published/validated need neither — a naive rank check was caught live wrongly flagging 7 real 'published' playbooks pointing at merely-'validated' routes (both load with zero flags, always fine) before it shipped. (3) validate_playbook_candidate gained an optional route_yaml input: supplying it certifies the playbook + route pair together, reporting pair_qualifies_for as the lower of each side's own structural DoD ceiling, and pair_status_mismatch:true with a plain blocking sentence — never a throw — when the playbook's declared status is already ahead of its route's. Locked by tests/registry/registryLoader.test.ts (drives the exact LAB failure plus a regression guard for a truly-unknown route id), tests/registry/registryLint.test.ts (the new gate, including the published/validated non-violation case), and 7 new cases in tests/tools/validatePlaybookCandidate.test.ts. pnpm verify: 2358/2358.
Explicit invoice-payment instructions now deterministically require human approval without fuzzy-matching ordinary phrases such as pay attention.

Goal-constraint phrase tables were matched with bare String.includes, so a phrase sitting inside a longer word counted as if the user had written it. 'posts the result in the same THREAD ONLY after I approve' contains 'read only' (th-read only) and fired the read-only prohibition on a goal that explicitly asks the agent to POST, degrading constraint_label to gaps; 'unread only', 'spread only', 'thread-only', 'no written approval' and 'preview before' (vs the approval phrase 'review before') failed the same way. Matching is now whole-word via (?<!\w)...(?!\w) lookarounds in src/lib/constraintSignals.ts, shared by constraintCoverage's own firstMatch. Inflections that substring matching had covered implicitly are now ENUMERATED in the tables (never writes, never edits/editing, never commits/committing) so a reader can see exactly what fires. The chat_triggered_assistant golden fixture's coverage_tags: ['read_only'] was a mislabel produced by this bug and is corrected.

An Airtable WRITE goal was planned as a READ. airtable_lookup is read-only (permissions.write is [], Connect entry 'Airtable - read base', required scopes data.records:read / schema.bases:read), but the bare `airtable` KEYWORD_HINT carried no direction, so 'write the output to an Airtable base' composed scheduled_trigger -> db_read -> airtable_lookup -> ... with NO write component in the route at all, and the plan told the user to provision a read-only token for a task needing writes. Two of four probed write goals were worse: 'append each new lead to our Airtable table' and 'update the status field in Airtable when a deal closes' made crm_note_write (a HubSpot/Salesforce note) the only write in the route - a write to a system the user never named. Approval provenance, from LAB's day-one signal intake (MAR-532): five separate partial plans all matched human_approval_gate + audit_log and all missed binding an approval to the exact action executed. ASSESSED AS BOTH a component gap and an edge gap. Mechanism = component gap: the gate's declared output is 'approved | rejected | timeout', a decision with no identity attached to what was decided, and audit_log takes the executed payload with no reference to an approved one, so no consumer can compare them; the drift failure modes appear in neither component's failure_modes (the gate records the HUMAN failing to read, not the system executing something else). Invisibility = edge gap, and it is concrete: of 163 real edges (164 files, one of which is _template.edge.yaml), human_approval_gate has ZERO outgoing edges (13 point at it, none leave it), and its own YAML's recommended_with: audit_log exists in the component file and NOT in the graph - route composition orders these components but never relates them. Sequence is not provenance. Worse than 'no component': a goal explicitly asking for 'an audit trail proving what I approved is exactly what ran' returns approval '✅ enforced' with unmatched_demand [] - a green check no fixture backs. NOT IMPLEMENTED deliberately: the hint-reachable shape is one slice but serves only users who already know to ask, leaving the default overclaim untouched and entrenching the wrong shape; the correct augmenter-injected shape changes every gated plan's route and ripples through the suite, EXPECTED_RELEASE_FINGERPRINT, the MAR-426 manifest fixture, benchmarks/public/*, the golden journeys and the DASH round-trip fixtures - not one slice. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08, PR #175 open against master, NOT merged. Two defects; the silent one is the serious one. DEFECT 1: '...write the leads to a spreadsheet WITH A SOURCE LINK ON EVERY ROW' returned unmatched_demand [] on a route that records no source link — the requirement was never REGISTERED as demand, not merely unsatisfied. Neither 'source' (only the plural 'sources' was listed) nor 'link' nor 'attribution' nor 'provenance' was vocabulary, and the clause opens with the determiner 'a', which MAR-396's shape detector rejects as a verb candidate — both paths to being heard were closed. Adding the vocabulary alone would NOT have fixed it: data_normalizer fuzzy-matches the bare word 'source' out of its own summary prose, and isClaimed's containment rule let that single word claim the whole phrase 'source link', so the ask would have been heard and immediately dismissed. Multi-word demand units now need a claim that is itself multi-word (file_storage's 'google sheet' hint still claims 'google sheets'; a lone 'source' no longer claims 'source link'). DEFECT 2: data_scraper was reachable only through scrape/crawl/extract — words naming the ACCESS PATTERN, not the outcome — so 'track competitor ad listings' composed no extraction step, and 'track competitor prices across their product pages every morning' composed scheduled_trigger -> state_store with no monitor either, because nothing established the monitoring domain and page_monitor's own 'product page' hint could not fire without it. Split by what the OBJECT is rather than by the verb: a LISTING is a record to collect (data_etl -> data_scraper), a PRICE or PAGE is a thing to watch for change (monitoring -> page_monitor). Both bump with the goal's OWN matched words as the token so coverage credits 'competitor'/'listings' by the words the user wrote (MAR-541's naming discipline) — without that the plan would report its own extraction step as uncovered. TWO EXCLUSIONS caught by existing fixtures before shipping: 'scan' is codebase_scan's verb and 'changes' is code vocabulary; together they reached the monitoring domain through 'scan a codebase, plan changes' and put a web-page monitor with a Firecrawl connection onto a code-review plan (MAR-117's credential-advisory fixture failed). BAR #2: data_extraction_route_v1 stops at schema_validation and the edge schema_validation__produces__file_storage was used by NO route at all; scheduled_extraction_to_storage + scheduled_extraction_to_storage_route_v1 (beta, live-probed) is its first named home. BAR #3 RECORDED DECISION: source_attribution is deliberately NOT composed in — its declared interface is answer-SPAN attribution over retrieved knowledge chunks, not row-level capture of where a scraped record came from, and wiring it in would be a coverage overclaim of the kind MAR-540 names. What is true is narrower and now written where it belongs: data_scraper's own declared output is 'list of raw extracted records WITH SOURCE URL and scrape timestamp', so the link exists at extraction and nothing downstream declares it survives — hence provenance is a guardrail and an eval on the new route rather than a claim. Controls hold: data_scraper__avoid__external_publish is carried by the new route and external_publish excluded; anti-detection scraping stays out of scope, stated in the playbook's avoid_when. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08, PR #176 open against master, NOT merged. Three independent build-or-decline calls; the issue named one of them the must-fix and that is what ships as code. MUST-FIX: 'pull invoices from the QuickBooks API on a schedule, KEEPING THE OAUTH TOKEN REFRESHED, and email a PDF report' reported unmatched_demand []. Nothing in that route performs a scheduled pre-expiry refresh, and auth_failure_handler says so itself — its declared INPUT is a 'failure signal from an external integration step (HTTP 401/403, expired token, missing scope)'. It absorbed the ask by fuzzy-matching the bare word 'token' out of its detect_token_expiry capability, and one claimed word clears a clause: the plan asserted coverage of a capability the registry does not have, the same overclaim shape MAR-540 records for approval binding. For an attended flow the difference barely shows; for the unattended nightly job the signal question describes, a refresh that only happens after a 401 means every run starts by failing, and a refresh token that expired BETWEEN runs means the job is dead until someone notices. Fixed with a rule keyed on the COMPONENT that would satisfy it (PROACTIVE_REFRESH_COMPONENTS, empty because nothing declares proactive refresh) rather than on a phrase claim, which the same 'token' claim would have dismissed. ITEM 1 Notion: component request filed as MAR-559 with an acceptance bar rather than built — unlike local_file_read (MAR-550, built this session, no credential at all), a Notion write is a CREDENTIALED external write needing a real COMPONENT_CONNECTIONS entry with scopes, a dashBrokerCatalog decision, and MAR-538's recorded limit (a missing connection entry renders a Connect row labelled with the wrong provider) is a live warning for it. ITEM 2 EDI 850: DECLINED with the reason stated — EDI 850 is an X12 interchange document whose envelopes, segment usage and qualifier codes are negotiated per trading partner, and a component claiming to generate one without conformance testing against a real partner would be an overclaim whose failure mode (an ERP silently rejecting a malformed 850) looks like a working agent. ITEM 3 proactive lifecycle: request filed as MAR-560 with the PRIOR question stated rather than presumed — is it a component at all, or a property of the connection contract? Every credentialed route needs it, and making it hint-reachable serves only users who already know to ask, the mistake MAR-540 names about approval_binding. Locked by tests/graph/tokenLifecycleDemand.test.ts (9 assertions, presence + absence, plus a regression guard that the Notion and EDI gaps stay REPORTED and no component quietly appears claiming to serve them). pnpm verify: 2541/2541.

issues.note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08, PR open against master, NOT merged. orchestratedash ADR 0008 slice 4 — the panel emitter, and the slice that RESTORES portfolio-wide verification: local `pnpm verify` had been stopping at `dash:schema:check` since DASH PR #85 (`3666459`) added $defs.panel/panelSectionV1/panelSectionOpaque/roleName and agent_dom.properties.panel, five drift paths the pinned fixture did not have. Fixture, contract.lock.json hashes and canonical_commit all move in ONE commit, which is what the check demands by design; the v2 semantic fingerprint goes da37810e -> bbd683e7 and canonical_commit 397a376 -> 3666459 (DASH master, confirmed clean against the commit before copying, per the MAR-499 lesson about copying from a sibling working tree). export_build_brief gains one optional `agent_panel` input, a .strict() zod mirror of DASH's $defs.panel including its if/then/else version split (panel_version 1 = the closed five-type enum; any other version = structurally-checked opaque sections that travel intact), threaded into agent_dom.panel conditionally — omitted when undeclared, never {}, which DASH's own schema refuses anyway since `sections` is required with minItems 1. PANEL_SECTION_TYPES_V1 is pinned by value in src/lib/observabilityContract.ts and asserted against the fixture's enum, so DASH widening the vocabulary turns this repo red on the next re-sync instead of widening it silently. THE DECISION WORTH READING: ADR 0008 PERMITS a derivation ('the emitter MAY derive a default panel … an output_location-bearing route gets a single report section') and docs/ADR-MAR-555-agent-panel-emission.md DECLINES it, on the MAR-549 recorded-decline precedent. Every v1 section that renders an agent's output binds to an artifact ROLE; a role is the name the agent's RUNTIME gives what it writes (DASH resolves it through describeArtifactRole(artifact.kind), whose whole known vocabulary is `digest` and `draft`), and a plan declares none. output_location is free text naming a DESTINATION ('HubSpot notes + Gmail drafts') that does not even satisfy roleName's ^[a-z0-9_]+$ — deriving a role from it would be the emitter inventing a binding the agent never promised, the exact overclaim class MAR-540/549/551 closed the same week. The one binding-free candidate (an `outputs` section with no artifact_role) is a quieter guess, not a grounded one: an output_location says output lands somewhere, often entirely outside DASH, not that this agent writes DASH artifacts at all. The decline is asserted, not just documented — 'the recorded decline' case pins that an output_location-bearing export still emits no panel, so anyone wiring derivation up later has to argue for it there. Registry untouched, so the fingerprint stays a59ee01fa6e99a1a and no benchmark/MAR-426-fixture bookkeeping was needed. Also fixed in passing: tests/fixtures/dash/README.md restated the v2 pinned commit and fingerprint inline and had been stale for two re-syncs (claimed 163f4141/2e9b3c8a while contract.lock.json said 397a376/da37810e); it now points at contract.lock.json as the single authority instead of duplicating values that drift.
